annotationRationale: The essential geometry is locating the center using equal chords and comparing right triangles formed by perpendicular chord bisectors. The supplied references all use this same route, so a second version would repeat the argument.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The equal chords must occupy adjacent lines: placing them on the outer lines would make the shorter middle chord a diameter. Comparing radius squares gives 72=2h², hence h=6, choice B. The stem, choices and key agree; no figure is needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2021_AMC_10B_Q14/compare-chord-right-triangles was independently checked and retained. Its statement is mathematically identical despite the recorded choicesMatch flag. LIVE and Random Math use the same chord-distance comparison, so no useful distinct route is omitted.
review.annotationCheck: Assessing cnm_251 and supporting it with cnm_174 correctly describes the argument. Replacing the previous chord-formula target with its explicitly used elementary geometry is appropriate.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Distinct parallel equal-chord lines place the center midway between them. The outer-line arrangement is correctly excluded. The remaining distances are h/2 and 3h/2, so 19²−17²=2h²=72; h>0 selects 6.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The exact shared question and method are credited, and both inherited reference IDs are preserved. The current LIVE and Random Math explanations also support this route. Reuse of the project-authored explanation and the source-informed-original designation are honest; no official MAA authorship is asserted.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation motivates using equal chords, derives the half-chord relation, and resolves the potentially ambiguous arrangement before calculating. A learner can reconstruct the geometry without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_251 supplies perpendicular chord bisection; cnm_174 supplies the radius-square equations. Both directly match the derivation.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native chord-bisection and Pythagorean topics apply. The problem does not test the arc-bisection portion of cnm_251.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.B.7 supports the right-triangle calculation. G-C.A.2 provides related chord geometry, but its supplied wording does not explicitly state the perpendicular chord-bisection theorem. This is component alignment, not full standard coverage.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Both immediate nodes are precise and sufficient. The derived equal-chord distance property needs no additional node.
